main_text.p: Nec poteft calcinari facile, quia sul-phur ejus cum hydrargyro pertinaciter eft conjunctum; quod non fit in stanno, ubi sulphur facilius effugit, & calcem re-linquit.
Ob spiritus terreos acres, calcinat aurum & argentum vivum cogit.
Argento familiare eft, & hydrargy-rum absumitur promte, & per artem e-tiam vertitur.
Differt a stanno immundicie majore, humiditate, difficultate calcinationis, & copia majore sulphuris constantis.
Ejus naturae accedit Antimonii, ma-gis terrestre, foetidu, arsenicale & rapax.
Metalla imperfecta dura sunt, quae ob siccum & terrestre sulphur, hydrargy-rumq; induratum igniuntur, antequam fundantur.Metalla imperfecta dura
Horum sulphur plus habet vitriolati succi.
Itaq; magis ferreum est & crassum, potestq; utrumq; in se mutuo verti, & ex utroq; elici multum chalcanthi.

page.notes: The catchword "igne" stands at the right below the last line and is given only in bottom_margin. The marginal note was read from a small italic print and is reasonably clear. The page number "183" is printed in a slightly unusual form at the top right and may have a long s; read here as 183. The word "immundicie" is read from a faint print and could be "immunditie" [?].
